name: Dawnlight Industries PurityMist PM-4 'Angel Breath'
description:
A premium chemical defense spray marketed to upper-tier residents who want personal protection without the stigma of carrying a weapon. The PM-4 dispenses a precisely metered dose of synthetic capsaicinoid in a fine mist from an elegant brushed-titanium canister designed to resemble a luxury perfume atomizer. The formulation includes a proprietary calming pheromone blend that Dawnlight claims reduces the user's own stress response during deployment.

The PM-4's active compound is a synthetic analog of capsaicin that Dawnlight developed to avoid the inconsistent potency of natural pepper extracts. The result is a spray with extremely predictable effects: exactly six minutes of incapacitating pain and blindness, followed by complete symptom resolution within twenty minutes. This predictability is the product's key selling point — it incapacitates reliably without causing the prolonged suffering or potential complications associated with cheaper formulations.

Dawnlight prices the PM-4 at Φ280 per canister — expensive enough to be aspirational, cheap enough for Tier 3 and above. The canister is refillable at Dawnlight boutiques located in Tier 3-5 commercial districts, where the refill service includes a complimentary deployment technique refresher. The entire experience is designed to feel like a spa visit rather than a weapons purchase.
specifications: capacity: 6 precision bursts range: 2 meters fine mist cone incapacitation duration: exactly 6 minutes full recovery: 20 minutes weight: 85 g canister material: brushed titanium refill cost: Φ45 at Dawnlight boutiques
tactical_use: The PM-4 is designed for close-range encounters — its fine mist disperses quickly beyond two meters. Dawnlight recommends a single burst aimed at the upper face, followed by immediate withdrawal. The spray's predictable six-minute incapacitation window gives the user a known timeframe to reach safety. Not recommended for multiple-attacker scenarios due to limited capacity.
cultural_context: The PM-4 is a status symbol disguised as a self-defense tool. Carrying one signals that you can afford to live in a tier where personal defense is a lifestyle accessory rather than a survival necessity. Dawnlight's boutique refill service has become a social ritual in Tier 3-4 communities — a place to be seen, to demonstrate that you take personal safety seriously without being gauche about it. Lower-tier residents mock the PM-4 as 'rich people's pepper spray,' but its formulation is genuinely superior to budget alternatives.
story_hooks: Dawnlight's calming pheromone blend has been found to contain a mild euphoric compound that creates subtle brand loyalty — users feel slightly better every time they handle their PM-4, associating the product with positive emotions.

A Tier 4 socialite deployed her PM-4 against an augmented mugger and it had no effect — the synthetic capsaicinoid doesn't trigger the same receptors as natural capsaicin in individuals with certain genetic modifications.

physical_description.visual_profile: An elegant, elongated atomizer that could pass for high-end fragrance at first glance — refined and aspirational rather than utilitarian. The form factor deliberately mimics luxury cosmetic design, with a tapered body and a delicate trigger mechanism that feels more like a perfume applicator than a defensive tool.
physical_description.dimensions: Height: 12.5 cm, Diameter: 3.2 cm at widest point (canister body), Trigger reach: 2.8 cm from canister surface
physical_description.weight_description: Light and balanced, 85 grams sits comfortably in a closed fist without fatigue — designed for extended carry in a pocket or clutch without noticeable burden. The weight distribution favors the hand, never feeling top-heavy despite the pressurized contents.
physical_description.primary_material: Brushed titanium canister body with precision-machined aluminum trigger assembly and sapphire-crystal metering valve window
physical_description.finish: Brushed titanium with a soft, non-reflective matte surface that catches light subtly rather than gleaming. Micro-etched grip panel with pearl-effect inlay that catches light when rotated. Anodized aluminum accents in soft silver-gray.
physical_description.color_scheme: Soft brushed titanium (cool silver-gray) with frosted translucent sapphire metering window showing pale opalescent liquid. Subtle pearl-gray grip inlay.
physical_description.grip_texture: Smoothly textured micro-etched titanium with a pearl-effect grip panel that provides subtle tactile feedback without appearing industrial — feels expensive and refined to the touch, with just enough texture to prevent slipping when sprayed.
distinctive_features: Sapphire-crystal metering valve window displaying remaining dose capacity and formulation color
Precision trigger with micro-click feedback at 50% and full depression
Dawnlight Industries signature engraved below the metering window in elegant serif font
Soft amber indicator light (hidden, activates on arm) near the trigger guard
Discrete serial number etched in micro-text on the bottom rim
Refill port caps the base with a quarter-turn bayonet lock
Aerosol release valve produces barely-audible hiss, far quieter than commercial pepper spray
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Dawnlight Industries logo (stylized ascending sun symbol) engraved below the metering window. Model designation 'PM-4' in micro-text on the trigger guard. 'Angel Breath' branding on the gift-box sleeve, not on the canister itself.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically pristine and showroom-ready — owners maintain these as luxury items. Light carry wear on grip panel edges possible after months of use. The brushed titanium shows fingerprints easily but resists scratching. Most PM-4s never see deployment.
